successors.name: Qin (state)
successors.text: the Yan lands taken by Qin in 226 (Ji and the plain) and 222 (Liaodong): 'The former Yan lands became the Liaodong Commandery, along with Yuyang, Beiping and Liaoxi' (Qin dossier quoting this event)…

successors.name: Han dynasty
successors.text: Zang Tu's united Yan kingdom (Yan and Liaodong), defeated by Liu Bang in 202; Lu Wan succeeds as King of Yan

capitals.name: Liaodong Peninsula (court in retreat; no city named)

rulers.name: Zang Tu
rulers.title: King of Yan (enfeoffed by Xiang Yu)

ledger.x: c. 1046: King Wu of Zhou enfeoffs the rulers of Yan, who rule from Liulihe near Beijing. After the Battle of Muye (c. 1046 BC) King Wu 'conferred titles to nobles within his domain, including the rulers of the Yan'; infobox 'Established: 11th century BC'. The page gives the capital (Liulihe, Fangshan District), not a…
7th century BC: Yan absorbs the small State of Ji and takes its city for its capital.
7th century BC: the capital moves from Liulihe to Ji (Xicheng District, Beijing); the page gives no year (placeholder for the century).

c. 300: General Qin Kai conquers the Liaodong Peninsula from Gojoseon. 'After returning to Yan, around 300 BC, he defeated the Donghu and conquered Liaodong Peninsula, wrestling it from Gojoseon.' Cliopatria's bigger Yan shape starts in 291; the keyframe yan_-300 carries it back to the page's date.
300: Yan's frontier advances against the Donghu.
284: Yue Yi of Yan sacks Linzi and Yan's allied army overruns Qi.
226: Qin takes Ji and the Yan plain.
226: the court leaves Ji for the Liaodong Peninsula.
222: Qin takes Liaodong and the Yan state ends.
209: Han Guang revives Yan after the Qin collapse.
206: Xiang Yu divides Han Guang's Yan.
206: Zang Tu kills Han Guang and unites Yan and Liaodong.
202: Zang Tu, who had rebelled against the Han Empire, is captured and executed; the kingdom of Yan passes to Lu Wan as a Han vassal.

wars.name: Qi invasion of Yan
wars.outcome: Qi overran Yan in 314 and was driven out after a revolt; King Zhao came to the throne in 312 (Yan page list; 311 on the King Zhao page).

wars.name: Qin Kai's campaign against the Donghu and Gojoseon
wars.outcome: Yan victory: the Donghu defeated, Liaodong wrested from Gojoseon.

wars.name: Yan-Zhao wars
wars.outcome: 'usually dragged on into a stalemate, requiring the help of other kingdoms to conclude.'

wars.name: Yue Yi's conquest of Qi
wars.outcome: Yan-led allied armies took Linzi in 284 and 'all but two' Qi cities; Yan held Qi until Qi was restored in 279.

wars.name: Qin conquest of Yan
wars.outcome: Jing Ke's failed assassination of the King of Qin (228 on the page, 227 on the Yan page) led to the fall of Ji in 226 and of Liaodong in 222.

wars.name: Zang Tu's revolt against Han
wars.outcome: Zang Tu invaded Dai around August 202, was defeated, captured around October and executed; Lu Wan became King of Yan.

certainty.note: Ancient frontiers named by cities and commanderies, never by survey; the Liaodong frontier after 300 is the softest.
Gap years 221-210 have no Yan; the revived kingdom's limits (from 209) are Cliopatria's and the Eighteen Kingdoms table's regional names.
